startup_note: 357 ms is the MEDIAN of 12 cold `bin/quill` launches from a shell to THE FIRST FRAME A HUMAN CAN SEE, with the 10,062-word document already in the profile (mean 369.6, sd 62.2, range 331.6-561.9; the 562 ms outlier is one run of the twelve and is in the raw data). It includes the chromium process spawn (159.6 ms of it), profile init, window creation, navigation, font loading and the full render. Round 2 published 322 ms here; that was `window.__quillReady`, a JS marker set at the end of Writer.boot() BEFORE any frame exists, and it was the smaller of the two numbers available. The equivalent marker this round is 273 ms (sd 8.7) and it is in detail.startup, labelled as a pre-paint marker. A brand-new profile - no code cache, no storage, a true first run - is 369 ms to first frame (median of 8). Inside an already-running browser a page load is 108 ms to first paint and 76 ms to the marker (n=12).
bar_note: iA Writer publishes no latency numbers at all. The bar is third-party: (1) 32.5 +/- 4.0 ms keyboard-to-photon for Sublime Text (Hume, photodiode, 60 Hz panel; TextEdit 33.4, Atom 45.6, VS Code 47.6), and (2) <=5 ms AVERAGE / <=16 ms WORST CASE app-internal keystroke->committed frame (REFERENCE 5.3; Fatin's Typometer means: Notepad++ 4.3, Emacs 5.3, Sublime 8.2). BOTH TOP-LEVEL FIELDS ABOVE ARE MEASURED END TO END with nothing cited added to them: keystroke -> presentation feedback of the frame carrying it, on a real Hyprland 0.56.2 compositor at 60 Hz, 3 sessions x 300 keystrokes, plain writing at the end of a 10,062-word draft, n=900, mean 21.99 +/- 10.72. For a like-for-like photon comparison with Hume's 32.5 you must ADD ~4 ms of panel pixel response, which nobody can measure without a photodiode: ~28.8 ms at the median, ~26.0 at the mean. Two caveats this round will not paper over. (a) THE COMPOSITOR RAN ON A VIRTUAL HYPRLAND OUTPUT, not on the physical panel: its own commit->present hop measures 17.23 ms p50, a whole 60 Hz refresh interval, where round 1's single physical-panel session measured 5.0 ms for the same hop. If the panel behaves as it did then, the true figure is nearer 13 + 4. The honest statement is a BRACKET, roughly 17-29 ms to photons, not a point - and the top of that bracket already beats Hume's Sublime. A physical-panel run is implemented (bin/quill --panel N, behind an evdev idle guard) and was attempted 20 times over 45 minutes: the machine was in use for 18 of those checks, and when it finally went idle the Dell U2720Q had gone into standby and dropped its DisplayPort link, so Hyprland had no physical output at all (it substitutes a FALLBACK headless output). Log: shots/latency/r3-panel-attempt.log. (b) The spread is wider than Hume's: sd 10.72 against 4.0, and the p99 of 36.5 is the VS Code bracket. On the app-internal bar - the part a builder controls - QUILL DOES NOT CLEAR IT: 5.73 ms mean (95% CI 5.50-5.95) against <=5, and 14.25 ms worst against <=16, on the headline regime; 8 of 11 paced regimes clear the worst case and none clears the average. Round 2 claimed this bar was cleared by quoting a p50 of 5.67 and a p99 of 14.99; the mean of the samples it shipped was 6.94 and its worst was 17.34. Full arithmetic: progress/latency-report.md sections 4-9.
method: Per keystroke, from Chrome's own EventTiming trace records (devtools.timeline, unrounded, microseconds), five milestones instead of two: the app's JavaScript returning, the wait for Chromium's next BeginFrame, the frame painted, commitFinishTime, and presentation feedback. Twelve regimes x 300 keystrokes x 3 sessions headless, three regimes x 300 x 3 on a real Hyprland compositor, on a real 10,062-word Markdown document with the caret on screen, 25 warm-up keys discarded. The typist presses real prose - capitals, punctuation, quotes, Enter, Backspace, undo, Ctrl+V paste, select-and-replace and Markdown syntax including opening and closing fenced code blocks - each keystroke labelled by kind and reported separately. Every regime asserts keydowns expected == keydowns in the trace == keydowns seen by an independent in-page rAF/MessageChannel probe, and that all of them carry commit and presentation times: true for all 36 headless, all 36 application-cost and all 9 compositor runs; nothing withheld. Application cost is measured under prefers-reduced-motion with no frame clock (the app's own caret glide is an animation, and an animation is a frame clock); the headless 60 Hz figure keeps a 1 px composited animation running so headless models a panel. EVERY BAR COMPARISON IS ANSWERED IN THE STATISTIC THE BAR IS STATED IN - mean, sd and worst case, with a bootstrap 95% CI on the mean - because Fatin's figures are means and Hume's is a mean +/- sd; p50/p99 are printed beside them, never instead of them. Statistics over fewer than 20 samples print n/mean/worst and no percentiles. Also measured: how much spare time a keystroke actually has (pure busy-wait injected into every keystroke: up to 2 ms changes nothing at all), CPU throttled 2x and 4x, four document sizes to 55k words, a 2,500-keystroke session with autosave and GC accounting, an idle frame-production control, cold starts that spawn a browser process per run, the deferred-render correctness suite, and the caret's own lag. Chromium 151.0.7922.173, i5-13600K, app fingerprint 6c61caa21c576e13, frozen snapshot server on port 4179. Full method, caveats and raw runs: progress/latency-report.md.

environment.panel: Dell U2720Q 3840x2160 @ 59.997 Hz - asleep, DisplayPort link down, during the window in which the machine was idle enough to measure on it
environment.compositor_output: virtual Hyprland headless output, 1920x1080 @ 60 Hz, created and removed by bin/quill; nothing shown on the physical screen
environment.served_from: frozen snapshot of app/ on port 4179

document.source: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (Project Gutenberg #11), one paragraph per line, italics as Markdown emphasis, an editor's note with a task list, a link, inline code and a fenced code block - shots/latency/doc10k.md

bar_app_internal.definition: keystroke hardware timestamp -> commitFinishTime of the frame carrying it, text-affecting keystrokes only, no display cadence, prefers-reduced-motion

round2_for_comparison.note: recomputed by the round-2 critic from shots/latency/r2-appcost.json; round 2 reported it as p50 5.67 / p99 14.99 and called it inside the bar

one_keystroke_taken_apart_ms.note: frame_wait in the raw files (mean 3.83 ms here) is JS-done -> the frame's first paint op: the wait for Chromium's next BeginFrame plus that frame's style, layout and pre-paint.

where_the_work_goes_us_per_key.note: nested trace events, so nothing is double counted. 'layout Quill forces by measuring the caret' is work the frame would have done anyway, moved earlier.

spare_time_in_a_keystroke.what: pure busy-wait added to every input event, after the app's own listener; keystroke -> committed frame, 10k words, 150 keys per arm
spare_time_in_a_keystroke.finding: up to 2 ms of extra work per keystroke does not move the committed-frame time at all; 4 ms costs 0.8 ms and 8 ms costs 4.7. The keystroke is scheduler-bound, not work-bound, so removing application work below the slack buys nothing.

input_delivery.how_keys_were_injected: CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent for every number in this file
input_delivery.what_that_excludes: the kernel -> libinput -> compositor -> client hop, so the photon arithmetic above is optimistic by that much
input_delivery.instrument_built: tools/uinput-keys.py creates a real keyboard on /dev/uinput and records CLOCK_MONOTONIC immediately before each write(2); Chromium's TimeTicks are CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux (verified: 813 us between a pre-dispatch clock_gettime and the trace's own keydown for that key). bin/quill --uinput drives it. It refuses to inject unless the page itself reports keyboard focus, and it only means anything on a focused window on the physical panel, which this round could not get.

autosave.note: files.js flushes the whole document to localStorage 400 ms after the last change; a run that never pauses never triggers it.

launcher_cold_editor_ready_marker_ms.note: window.__quillReady, a JS marker set at the end of Writer.boot() BEFORE any frame exists. Not the headline.

caret_lag_ms.what: keydown -> the caret's box has stopped moving, at 133 wpm (shots/latency/probes/caret-glide.mjs). app/js/caret.js glides the caret over GLIDE_X = 62 ms whenever two keystrokes are more than SNAP_MS = 60 ms apart, which at any ordinary writing speed is every keystroke.
caret_lag_ms.note: The glyph is on the glass in ~6 ms. This is the largest perceptible latency in the product and the one thing a typist's eye is actually on; against Dan Luu's 2 ms threshold it is not close. app/js/caret.js belongs to another piece; reported for the second round running.

idle_control.what: idle page, no keystrokes at all, display clock on
idle page, no keystrokes at all, display clock off
